   303	/-! ## Observable-distance normalization -/
   304	
   305	/-- The affine operator `(1 ± S)/2`, which is the effect of a binary projective
   306	measurement when `S` is a binary observable.
   307	The two effects are `(1 + O) / 2` and `(1 - O) / 2`. -/
   308	noncomputable def binaryObservableEffect {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   309	    [DecidableEq ι] (outcome : Bool) (O : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   310	  if outcome then ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 - O) else ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 + O)
   311	
   312	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance of two operators, summed over the two
   313	effects `(1 ± O)/2`; when both operators are binary observables this is the
   314	squared distance between the associated binary projective measurements.  This is the measurement
   315	distance calculated in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`; its relation
   316	to `stateDepDistSq` is recorded in
   317	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   318	noncomputable def binaryObservableDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   319	    [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
   320	  ∑ outcome : Bool,
   321	    stateDepDistSq (binaryObservableEffect outcome S)
   322	      (binaryObservableEffect outcome T) ρ
   323	
   324	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance is half the squared
   325	state-dependent operator distance.
   326	
   327	**Local fix:** Source equation (3) at
   328	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:903-911` ends by identifying the squared
   329	binary-measurement distance with the squared state-dependent operator distance
   330	of the two observables; the correct relation carries the factor `1 / 2` proved
   331	here.
   332	Documented in
   333	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   334	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two
   335	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) :
   336	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ = stateDepDistSq S T ρ / 2 := by
   337	  simp only [binaryObservableDistSq, Fintype.univ_bool, stateDepDistSq,
   338	    binaryObservableEffect, smul_add, Matrix.conjTranspose_sub,
   339	    Finset.mem_singleton, Bool.true_eq_false, not_false_eq_true,
   340	    Finset.sum_insert, reduceIte, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_inv₀,
   341	    star_ofNat, Matrix.conjTranspose_one, Finset.sum_singleton,
   342	    Bool.false_eq_true, Matrix.conjTranspose_add, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]
   343	  have hminusStar :
   344	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Sᴴ) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Tᴴ) =
   345	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ)) := by
   346	    module
   347	  have hminus :
   348	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - S) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - T) =
   349	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T)) := by
   350	    module
   351	  have hplusStar :
   352	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Sᴴ - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Tᴴ =
   353	        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ) := by
   354	    module
   355	  have hplus :
   356	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • S - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • T =
   357	        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T) := by
   358	    module
   359	  rw [hminusStar, hminus, hplusStar, hplus]
   360	  simp only [neg_mul, mul_neg, neg_neg, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul]
   361	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   362	  ring
   363	
   364	/-- The state-dependent squared distance between binary observables in terms
   365	of their correlation. -/
   366	theorem stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation
   367	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   368	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   369	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   370	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   371	    stateDepDistSq S T ρ =
   372	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   373	  have hstar :
   374	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   375	    calc
   376	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace ((S * T * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   377	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   378	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * T * S) := by
   379	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq, hρ.isHermitian.eq,
   380	          Matrix.mul_assoc]
   381	      _ = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   382	        exact (Matrix.trace_mul_cycle T S ρ).symm
   383	  have hcross :
   384	      (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re = (Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ)).re := by
   385	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   386	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   387	  have hdiff :
   388	      (S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) =
   389	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   390	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq]
   391	    calc
   392	      (S - T) * (S - T) = S * S - S * T - T * S + T * T := by
   393	        noncomm_ring
   394	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   395	        rw [hS.2, hT.2]
   396	        module
   397	  unfold stateDepDistSq
   398	  rw [hdiff]
   399	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   400	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   401	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   402	  rw [hcross]
   403	  ring
   404	
   405	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance is one minus the real
   406	state-dependent correlation. -/
   407	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_one_sub_correlation
   408	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   409	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   410	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   411	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   412	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ =
   413	      1 - (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   414	  rw [binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two,
   415	    stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation S T ρ hS hT hρ htrace]
   416	  ring
   417	
   418	end
   419	
   420	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Binary observables and the state-dependent distance
     6	
     7	This file collects the notions in which the quantum linearity theorem of
     8	Natarajan and Vidick is stated: binary observables, the rank-one density
     9	operator of an ancillary vector, and the squared state-dependent distance
    10	between two operators weighted by a positive semidefinite trace-one operator.
    11	The theorem itself, `exists_exactly_linear_observables`, is stated and proved
    12	in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean` from the Boolean Fourier,
    13	operator BLR, Naimark rounding, and representation stability modules under
    14	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/`, all of which build on this file.
    15	
    16	## Main definitions
    17	
    18	* `IsBinaryObservable`: a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    19	* `ancProj`: the rank-one density operator `|v⟩⟨v|` of a vector `v`.
    20	* `stateDepDistSq`: the squared state-dependent distance
    21	  `d_ρ(S, T)^2 = Re Tr((S - T)^† (S - T) ρ)`.
    22	
    23	## References
    24	
    25	The notions are those of `thm:linearity` in
    26	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`, quoted in the QPBT
    27	paper at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`
    28	from Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574,
    29	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1088`; the state-dependent distance is
    30	defined there at lines 866--875.
    31	-/
    32	
    33	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    34	
    35	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    36	
    37	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    38	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    39	
    40	noncomputable section
    41	
    42	/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    43	This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    44	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`, quoted at paper
    45	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
    46	def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    47	    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
    48	  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1
    49	
    50	/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector.  This
    51	is the state `|anc⟩⟨anc|` of the extension `ρ' = ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` in
    52	`thm:linearity`, blueprint
    53	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`. -/
    54	noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    55	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
    56	  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v
    57	  Matrix.vecMulVec w (star w)
    58	
    59	/-- Squared state-dependent distance between two operators.  This is the
    60	quantity `d_ρ(S,T)^2` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    61	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`, the state-dependent
    62	distance of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`. -/
    63	noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    64	    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    65	  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re
    66	
    67	end
    68	
    69	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# The operator-valued BLR bound
     6	
     7	This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
     8	linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
     9	indexed by the Boolean cube `𝔽_2^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
    10	operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
    11	family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
    12	sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
    13	overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` used in the
    14	Naimark-dilation argument.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
    15	assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.
    16	
    17	## Main results
    18	
    19	* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
    20	  from `O^{u+v}`.
    21	* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
    22	  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
    23	  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
    24	  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
    25	* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
    26	  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
    27	* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
    28	  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.
    29	
    30	## References
    31	
    32	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
    33	its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
    34	distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
    35	the theorem at
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
    37	invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    38	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81-147`.  The normalization of
    39	the error constant is analyzed in
    40	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
    41	bound is `2 * δ` for the squared state-dependent operator distance
    42	`stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for the squared binary-observable distance.
    43	-/
    44	
    45	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    46	
    47	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    48	
    49	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    50	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    51	
    52	noncomputable section
    53	
    54	/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
    55	
    56	/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
    57	uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `𝔽_2^t`, of the real part of
    58	`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
    59	Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
    60	quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
    61	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
    62	the one used there. -/
    63	def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    64	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    65	  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    66	    (fun pair =>
    67	      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
    68	
    69	/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
    70	namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
    71	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
    72	`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
    73	quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,
    74	measured with the squared state-dependent operator distance
    75	`stateDepDistSq`. -/
    76	def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    77	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
    78	  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ
    79	
    80	/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
    81	defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
    82	expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
    83	triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
    84	adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
    85	equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
    86	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
    87	family. -/
    88	theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
    89	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    90	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
    91	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    92	    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    93	    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
    94	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
    95	  have hu := hO u
    96	  have hv := hO v
    97	  have huv := hO (u + v)
    98	  have hdiff :
    99	      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   100	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   101	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
   102	      huv.1.eq]
   103	    calc
   104	      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   105	          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   106	            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
   107	        noncomm_ring
   108	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   109	            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   110	        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
   111	        module
   112	  have hstar :
   113	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   114	        Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   115	    calc
   116	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   117	          Matrix.trace ((O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   118	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   119	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * (O v * O u * O (u + v))) := by
   120	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
   121	          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   122	      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   123	        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
   124	  have hcross :
   125	      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
   126	        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by
   127	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   128	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   129	  unfold multiplicativeDefect stateDepDistSq
   130	  rw [hdiff]
   131	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   132	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   133	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   134	  rw [hcross, add_comm v u]
   135	  ring
   136	
   137	/-- The average multiplicative defect over a uniformly random pair equals
   138	`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The pointwise identity
   139	`multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` produces the correlation
   140	summand with the two variables in reversed order; since the pair is uniform,
   141	exchanging the two coordinates leaves the average unchanged.  This is the
   142	relation between the approximate-linearity hypothesis of the QPBT quotation
   143	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`) and
   144	display (7) of Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`),
   145	in the operator-distance normalization of
   146	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   147	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
   148	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   149	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   150	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1) :
   151	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   152	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   153	      2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   154	  have hswap :
   155	      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   156	        (fun pair =>
   157	          (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) =
   158	        blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   159	    unfold blrCorrelation
   160	    refine (avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) _).trans ?_
   161	    exact avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair => rfl)
   162	  calc
   163	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   164	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   165	        avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   166	          (fun pair => 2 - 2 *
   167	            (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) :=
   168	      avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair =>
   169	        multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace
   170	          pair.1 pair.2)
   171	    _ = 2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   172	      rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_uniform_const, hswap]
   173	
   174	/-- The operator-valued BLR bound: under the correlation hypothesis of
   175	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the average squared defect of `O^u O^v`
   176	from `O^{u+v}` is at most `2 * δ`.  This is the passage from display (7) of
   177	Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`) to the
   178	approximate-linearity relation of the QPBT quotation
   179	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`); the
   180	constant `2` is the operator-distance normalization recorded in
   181	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   182	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error {t : ℕ}
   183	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   184	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   185	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
   186	    (δ : ℝ) (hcorrelation : 1 - δ ≤ blrCorrelation O ρ) :
   187	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   188	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) ≤ 2 * δ := by
   189	  rw [avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace]
   190	  linarith
   191	
   192	/-! ## The cubic Fourier identity -/
   193	
   194	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier computations in the
   195	proof of Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick
   196	(`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1112`): a twisted form of the
   197	matrix-valued Parseval identity in which only the first factor is expanded
   198	through its Fourier coefficients.  Taking `a = 0` recovers Parseval. -/
   199	private theorem sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul {t : ℕ}

     3	/-!
     4	# Boolean representation stability
     5	
     6	This file completes the proof of the quantum linearity theorem of Natarajan
     7	and Vidick in its multiplicative-defect formulation.  A family of
     8	binary observables `O^u`, indexed by the Boolean cube `F_2^t` and weighted by a
     9	positive semidefinite trace-one operator `ρ`, whose products `O^u O^v` are on
    10	average close to `O^{u+v}` in the state-dependent distance, is on average close,
    11	in the same distance and weighted by the extended state `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`, to
    12	an exactly linear family of binary observables on an ancillary extension.
    13	
    14	The extension, the ancillary vector, and the exactly linear family are those
    15	of the Naimark rounding of the Fourier-square POVM.  The main computation is
    16	an identity, not an inequality: the average squared state-dependent operator
    17	distance between the rounded family and the ampliated original family,
    18	weighted by `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`, equals the average multiplicative defect of the
    19	original family weighted by `ρ`.  Both sides equal
    20	`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The left side reduces to the
    21	correlation by compressing the rounded observables along the ancillary vector
    22	and applying the cubic Fourier identity; the right side is the operator BLR
    23	computation, including the reindexing of the uniform pair.  No commutation
    24	among the observables is assumed, and the weight `ρ` is never replaced by the
    25	normalized trace.
    26	
    27	## Main results
    28	
    29	* `heteroKron_ancProj_posSemidef` and `trace_heteroKron_ancProj`: the extended
    30	  weight `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` is again positive semidefinite with trace one.
    31	* `re_trace_roundedObservable_mul_heteroKron`: the compression of the
    32	  correlation between a rounded observable and the ampliated original
    33	  observable to the original space.
    34	* `stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable`: the pointwise distance between a rounded
    35	  observable and the ampliated original observable, in terms of the overlap
    36	  with the character sum of the Fourier-square POVM.
    37	* `avg_stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable_eq_avg_multiplicativeDefect`: the
    38	  distance/defect identity
    39	  `E_u d_{ρ'}(L^u, O^u ⊗ 1)^2 = E_{u,v} d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2`.
    40	* `exists_exact_boolean_representation`: the Boolean representation stability
    41	  theorem, obtained by weakening the identity to the incoming bound.
    42	
    43	## References
    44	
    45	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 and its Fourier/Naimark
    46	proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the closing step, which
    47	converts the overlap certificate into the distance bound, is at lines
    48	1104--1112, and the state-dependent distance is defined at lines 866--900.
    49	The QPBT paper quotes the theorem at
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`.  The
    51	blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    52	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:98-147`, and the
    53	correlation-form statement is `exists_exactly_linear_observables` in
    54	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean`.  The declarations of this file are
    55	collected in the blueprint as `lem:boolean-representation-stability`.  The
    56	normalization convention, under which the incoming average multiplicative
    57	defect and the outgoing average squared state-dependent operator distance
    58	carry the same constant, is recorded in
    59	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`.
    60	-/
    61

   137	theorem re_trace_roundedObservable_mul_heteroKron {t : ℕ} {ι : Type}

    59	Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
    60	quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
    61	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
    62	the one used there. -/
    63	def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    64	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    65	  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))

    72	`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT

   277	    _ = (N⁻¹ * N⁻¹) • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   278	          O b * O c * O (b + c) := by
   279	      simp only [mul_smul_comm, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul,
   280	        Matrix.mul_assoc]
   281	    _ = ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   282	          ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
   283	            O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
   284	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul, mul_inv]
   285	
   286	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the averages in this file: a uniform
   287	average over a nonempty finite type is the sum divided by the cardinality. -/
   288	private theorem avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum {α : Type*}
   289	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (f : α → ℝ) :
   290	    avgOver (uniformDistribution α) f = (Fintype.card α : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ a, f a := by
   291	  simp [avgOver, uniformDistribution, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight,
   292	    Finset.mul_sum]
   293	
   294	/-- The sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients evaluated in `ρ` equals the
   295	two-query correlation:
   296	`∑_u Re Tr((hat O^u)^3 ρ) = E_{a,b} Re Tr(O^a O^b O^{a+b} ρ)`.  This is the
   297	identity stated at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1111-1112`, with the
   298	complex traces compared through their real parts. -/
   299	theorem operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation {t : ℕ}
   300	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   301	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) :
   302	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   303	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   304	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re =
   305	      blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   306	  rw [← Complex.re_sum, ← Matrix.trace_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul,
   307	    sum_operatorFourier_cube, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul, Finset.sum_mul,
   308	    Matrix.trace_sum]
   309	  unfold blrCorrelation
   310	  rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, smul_eq_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_natCast,
   311	    ← Complex.ofReal_inv, Complex.re_ofReal_mul, Complex.re_sum]

   313	/-! ## The Fourier-square POVM and its overlap certificate -/
   314	
   315	/-- Each Fourier square `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` of a Hermitian operator family is
   316	positive semidefinite, being the product of a Hermitian matrix with its
   317	adjoint.  This is the positivity half of the assertion that the `B^u` form a
   318	POVM at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1098-1099`. -/
   319	theorem operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef {t : ℕ}
   320	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   321	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, (O a).IsHermitian)
   322	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   323	    (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u).PosSemidef := by
   324	  have h := operatorFourier_isHermitian O hO u
   325	  simpa [h.eq] using
   326	    Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self (operatorFourier O u)
   327	
   328	/-- The Fourier-square POVM `{B^u = (hat O^u)^2}` of a family of binary
   329	observables, with outcomes in `𝔽_2^t`.  Positivity is
   330	`operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef` and completeness is the Parseval
   331	identity `sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one`.  This is the POVM to which Naimark's
   332	theorem is applied at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1097-1100`. -/
   333	def fourierSquareMeasurement {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   334	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   335	    Measurement (Fin t → ZMod 2) ι :=
   336	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   337	    (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)
   338	    (fun u => (operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef O (fun a => (hO a).1) u).nonneg)
   339	    (sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one O hO)
   340	
   341	/-- The effects of the Fourier-square POVM are the squares of the Fourier
   342	coefficients. -/
   343	@[simp]
   344	theorem fourierSquareMeasurement_effect {t : ℕ}
   345	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   346	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   347	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   348	    (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).effect u =
   349	      operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u :=
   350	  rfl
   351	
   352	/-- The average state-dependent overlap between `O^a` and the character sum
   353	`∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u` of the Fourier-square operators `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` equals
   354	the sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients evaluated in `ρ`.  The family `O` is
   355	arbitrary here, so the `B^u` need not be positive or sum to the identity; they
   356	are the effects of a POVM only under the binary-observable hypothesis of
   357	`fourierSquareMeasurement`.  This is the computation of
   358	`E_a Re Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1104-1110`,
   359	carried out before the Naimark dilation: the character sum is the compression
   360	of the exactly linear observable `𝒜(a) = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` to the original
   361	space. -/
   362	theorem avg_overlap_fourierSquare_eq_sum_cube {t : ℕ}
   363	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   364	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) :
   365	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   366	        (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
   367	          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   368	            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) =
   369	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   370	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   371	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re := by
   372	  classical
   373	  have hop :
   374	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   375	          operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
   376	        ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   377	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   378	            booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) := by
   379	    have := sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul O
   380	      (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) 0
   381	    simpa only [booleanCharacter_zero_right, one_smul, zero_add] using this
   382	  symm
   383	  calc
   384	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   385	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   386	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re =
   387	        (Matrix.trace ((∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   388	          operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) *
   389	            ρ)).re := by
   390	      rw [Finset.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum, Complex.re_sum]
   391	      simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
   392	    _ = (Matrix.trace ((((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   393	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   394	            booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) *
   395	              ρ)).re := by
   396	      rw [hop]
   397	    _ = (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   398	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, (Matrix.trace (O b *
   399	            (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u b •
   400	              (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re := by
   401	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul, Finset.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum,
   402	        smul_eq_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_natCast, ← Complex.ofReal_inv,
   403	        Complex.re_ofReal_mul, Complex.re_sum]
   404	    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   405	          (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
   406	            (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   407	              (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) := by
   408	      rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum]
   409	
   410	/-- The overlap certificate for the Fourier-square operators `B^u = (hat O^u)^2`:
   411	under the correlation hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the
   412	average state-dependent overlap between `O^a` and the character sum
   413	`∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u` is at least `1 - δ`.  The family `O` is arbitrary here, so
   414	the `B^u` are the effects of a POVM only under the binary-observable hypothesis
   415	of `fourierSquareMeasurement`.  This is the conclusion of the computation at
   416	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1104-1112` in the form used after the
   417	Naimark dilation: the same overlap, evaluated in `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` against the
   418	exactly linear observables, is what bounds the average distance in display (8).
   419	No commutation among the observables is used. -/
   420	theorem one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare {t : ℕ}
   421	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   422	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι)
   423	    (δ : ℝ) (hcorrelation : 1 - δ ≤ blrCorrelation O ρ) :
   424	    1 - δ ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   425	        (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
   426	          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   427	            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) := by
   428	  rw [avg_overlap_fourierSquare_eq_sum_cube,
   429	    operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation]

     4	/-!
     5	# Naimark rounding of the Fourier-square POVM
     6	
     7	This file carries out the dilation step in the proof of the quantum linearity
     8	theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  The Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2`
     9	of a family of binary observables `O^a`, indexed by the Boolean cube `F_2^t`,
    10	is dilated by the one-measurement Naimark construction of the low individual
    11	degree test to a projective measurement `{C^u}` on the enlarged space
    12	`ι × Option (F_2^t)`, whose compression along the canonical ancillary vector is
    13	again `{B^u}`.  The signed character sums `L^a = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` are then
    14	binary observables satisfying the exact linearity `L^a L^b = L^{a+b}`.
    15	
    16	The one-measurement Naimark construction produces a projective submeasurement
    17	indexed by `Option (F_2^t)`: one projector for each Fourier outcome and one for
    18	the residual outcome `none`.  Its projectors sum only to at most the identity,
    19	so the Fourier-indexed ones alone need not resolve the identity on the enlarged
    20	space, and the signed character sums of a family that does not resolve the
    21	identity are not multiplicative.  The zero Fourier outcome is therefore enlarged
    22	to the complement of the sum of the projectors attached to the nonzero outcomes;
    23	that complement is again a projector orthogonal to the others, and it absorbs
    24	the residual outcome.  Since the Fourier-square effects themselves sum to the
    25	identity, the enlarged zero projector still compresses to `B^0`.
    26	
    27	## Main definitions and results
    28	
    29	* `naimarkAncilla`, `norm_naimarkAncilla`, `ancProj_naimarkAncilla`: the
    30	  canonical ancillary unit vector and its rank-one density.
    31	* `roundedFourierPVM` with `roundedFourierPVM_isProj`,
    32	  `roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one`, `roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne`, and
    33	  `trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM`: the dilated family of projectors
    34	  and its compression to the Fourier-square POVM.
    35	* `roundedFourierMeasurement` with `roundedFourierMeasurement_effect` and
    36	  `roundedFourierMeasurement_isProjective`: the projective measurement with
    37	  outcomes in `F_2^t` whose effects are those projectors.
    38	* `roundedObservable` with `roundedObservable_mul` and
    39	  `roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable`: the exactly linear binary observables.
    40	* `trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedObservable`: the compression of the rounded
    41	  observables, in the form used to prove the averaged distance bound.
    42	
    43	## References
    44	
    45	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, proof of Theorem 10,
    46	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1104`: the Naimark dilation of `{B^u}`
    47	is at lines 1099--1100, the observables `𝒜(a) = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` at lines
    48	1100--1102, and their exact linearity at lines 1103--1104.  The QPBT paper
    49	quotes the theorem at
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`, and
    51	the blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    52	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:98-133`.  The one-measurement
    53	Naimark construction reused here is `oneMeasNaimark` in
    54	`MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/NaimarkOneMeas.lean`, with the
    55	associated dilation data defined in
    56	`MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/Defs.lean`.
    57	-/
    58	
    59	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    60	
    61	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    62	
    63	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    64	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    65	open MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective

    67	noncomputable section
    68	
    69	/-! ## The canonical ancillary vector -/
    70	
    71	/-- The canonical ancillary vector of the Naimark dilation: the basis vector of
    72	the residual index `none` in `Option (F_2^t)`.  This is the pure state `|anc⟩`
    73	of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`; in the one-measurement
    74	Naimark construction it is the initial state `|⊥⟩` of the auxiliary register. -/
    75	def naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
    76	  EuclideanSpace.single none 1
    77	
    78	/-- The canonical ancillary vector is a unit vector. -/
    79	theorem norm_naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) : ‖naimarkAncilla t‖ = 1 := by
    80	  simp [naimarkAncilla]
    81	
    82	/-- The rank-one density `|anc⟩⟨anc|` of the canonical ancillary vector is the
    83	auxiliary projector `|⊥⟩⟨⊥|` of the one-measurement Naimark construction. -/
    84	theorem ancProj_naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) :
    85	    ancProj (naimarkAncilla t) = naimarkAuxProjector (Fin t → ZMod 2) := by
    86	  ext i j
    87	  cases i <;> cases j <;>
    88	    simp [ancProj, naimarkAncilla, naimarkAuxProjector, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply]
    89	
    90	/-! ## The Naimark dilation of the Fourier-square POVM -/
    91	
    92	/-- The one-measurement Naimark dilation data of the Fourier-square POVM
    93	`{B^u}`, supplied by `oneMeasNaimark`: a family of projectors on
    94	`ι × Option (F_2^t)`, indexed by `Option (F_2^t)`, summing to at most the
    95	identity and reproducing every expectation value of `{B^u}` in the lifted
    96	state.  Only the inequality `∑ a, P̂_a ≤ 1` is available, so this is the
    97	projective submeasurement supplied by the one-measurement Naimark dilation of
    98	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`; completeness holds only once the
    99	zero Fourier outcome has been enlarged to the complement of the nonzero ones,
   100	and is recorded for the resulting projective measurement
   101	`roundedFourierMeasurement`. -/
   102	def fourierNaimarkData {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   103	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   104	    OneMeasNaimarkData (Fin t → ZMod 2) ι :=
   105	  Classical.choose (oneMeasNaimark (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement)
   106	
   107	/-- The Naimark dilation data of `fourierNaimarkData` dilates the Fourier-square
   108	POVM. -/
   109	theorem fourierNaimarkData_source {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   110	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   111	    (fourierNaimarkData O hO).source = (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement :=
   112	  Classical.choose_spec (oneMeasNaimark (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement)
   113	
   114	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the rounding below: distinct
   115	projectors of a one-measurement Naimark dilation are orthogonal, since they are
   116	projectors summing to at most the identity. -/
   117	private theorem liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne {α d : Type*}
   118	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   119	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) {a b : Option α} (hab : a ≠ b) :
   120	    data.liftedEffect a * data.liftedEffect b = 0 :=
   121	  data.toProjSubMeasOption.outcome_orthogonal a b hab
   122	
   123	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the compression identities below:
   124	the expectation-preservation identity of a one-measurement Naimark dilation,
   125	written with plain traces.  For every operator `X` on the original space,
   126	`Tr((X ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|) P̂_a) = Tr(X M_a)`. -/
   127	private theorem trace_kronecker_auxProjector_mul_liftedEffect {α d : Type*}
   128	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   129	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) (X : Op d) (a : α) :
   130	    Matrix.trace (Matrix.kronecker X (naimarkAuxProjector α) * data.liftedEffect (some a)) =
   131	      Matrix.trace (X * data.source.effect a) := by
   132	  have h := data.expectation_preservation X a
   133	  simp only [normalizedTrace, oneMeasLiftedDensity, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul,
   134	    smul_eq_mul, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul] at h
   135	  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty d with hd | hd
   136	  · simp [Matrix.trace]
   137	  · have hd0 : (Fintype.card d : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   138	    have hα : (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   139	    rw [mul_comm (Fintype.card d : ℂ), mul_div_mul_left _ _ hα, div_left_inj' hd0] at h
   140	    exact h.symm
   141	
   142	/-! ## Absorbing the residual outcome into the zero Fourier outcome -/
   143	
   144	/-- The rounded Fourier projectors `{C^u}` on `ι × Option (F_2^t)`, obtained
   145	from the Naimark dilation of the Fourier-square POVM by enlarging the zero
   146	Fourier outcome until it absorbs the residual outcome `none`.  For `u ≠ 0` the
   147	projector is the dilated projector of the outcome `u`; for `u = 0` it is the
   148	complement of the sum of the dilated projectors of the nonzero outcomes, so
   149	that the family resolves the identity on the enlarged space.  The measurement
   150	with outcomes in `F_2^t` whose effects are these projectors is
   151	`roundedFourierMeasurement`, the projective measurement `{C^u}` of
   152	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`. -/
   153	def roundedFourierPVM {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   154	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   155	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op (ι × Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
   156	  if u = 0 then
   157	    1 - ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v)
   158	  else (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some u)
   159	
   160	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
   161	dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes absorbs each of them on the
   162	left. -/
   163	private theorem sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   164	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   165	    {v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
   166	    (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) *
   167	        (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) =
   168	      (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) := by
   169	  rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.sum_eq_single v]
   170	  · exact ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some v)).isIdempotentElem.eq
   171	  · intro w _ hwv
   172	    exact liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne _ (fun h => hwv (Option.some_inj.mp h))
   173	  · intro hv'
   174	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hv, Finset.mem_univ v⟩) hv'
   175	
   176	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
   177	dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes is a projector, its summands
   178	being mutually orthogonal projectors. -/
   179	private theorem isProj_sum_erase {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   180	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   181	    IsProj (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) := by
   182	  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
   183	  · unfold IsIdempotentElem
   184	    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   185	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   186	    intro w hw
   187	    exact sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hw)
   188	  · rw [isSelfAdjoint_iff, star_sum]
   189	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   190	    intro w _
   191	    exact ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some w)).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
   192	
   193	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
   194	dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes absorbs each of them on the
   195	right, by taking adjoints in the left absorption. -/
   196	private theorem liftedEffect_mul_sum_erase {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   197	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))

+	Projections summing to at most the identity are mutually orthogonal, so
+	$\hat{P}_a \hat{P}_b = 0$ for $a \ne b$. Consequently
+	$Q = \sum_{v \ne 0} \hat{P}_v$ absorbs each of its summands on either
+	side, $Q \hat{P}_v = \hat{P}_v Q = \hat{P}_v$ for $v \ne 0$, whence $Q$ is
+	itself a projection and $C^0 = \Id - Q$ is a projection orthogonal to
+	every $\hat{P}_v$ with $v \ne 0$. Splitting off the zero outcome in
+	$\sum_u C^u$ leaves $(\Id - Q) + Q = \Id$.
+
+	For $u \ne 0$ the compression identity is the expectation-preservation
+	identity supplied with the dilation of Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper},
+	rewritten with unnormalized traces; the normalizing factors of the two
+	spaces cancel, the enlarged space having dimension
+	$(\lvert \F_2^t \rvert + 1)$ times that of $\hilb$. For $u = 0$,
+	linearity of the trace reduces the claim to
+	$\Tr(X \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}) = \Tr(X)$ together with
+	the identity $B^0 = \Id - \sum_{v \ne 0} B^v$, which is the completeness
+	$\sum_u B^u = \Id$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}.
+
+	Expanding $\mathcal{L}^a \mathcal{L}^b$ and using that $C^u C^v$ vanishes
+	for $u \ne v$ and equals $C^u$ for $u = v$ leaves the diagonal terms
+	$\sum_u \chi_u(a) \chi_u(b) \, C^u$, and
+	$\chi_u(a) \chi_u(b) = \chi_u(a+b)$ by
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-characters}. Taking $a = 0$ in the definition of
+	$\mathcal{L}^a$ and using $\chi_u(0) = 1$ gives
+	$\mathcal{L}^0 = \sum_u C^u = \Id$. Hermiticity of $\mathcal{L}^a$ follows
+	from the realness of the characters and the self-adjointness of the
+	$C^u$, and $(\mathcal{L}^a)^2 = \mathcal{L}^{a+a} = \mathcal{L}^0 = \Id$
+	because $a + a = 0$ in characteristic two, so each $\mathcal{L}^a$ is a
+	binary observable. The last identity is the compression identity for the
+	$C^u$ summed against the characters.
+\end{proof}

   208		\[

   217		\[
   218			U \cdot (\ket{\phi} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})
   219			=
   220			\sum_{a \in \mathcal A} ((A_a)^{1/2}\ket{\phi}) \ot \ket{a}

   230			(I-A)^{1/2} \ot \ket{\bot},

   234			(I \ot \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}})

    42	\section{Key theorem forms}
    43	
    44	Let $S$ and $T$ be binary observables and let $\rho$ be a positive
    45	semidefinite operator of trace one.  We distinguish the state-dependent
    46	operator distance from the distance between their associated binary projective
    47	measurements:
    48	\begin{align*}
    49	  d_\rho(S,T)^2
    50	    &:= \Re\tr\big((S-T)^\dagger(S-T)\rho\big), \\
    51	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
    52	    &:= \sum_{s\in\{+,-\}}
    53	      \Re\tr\big((P_S^s-P_T^s)^\dagger
    54	                       (P_S^s-P_T^s)\rho\big),
    55	  \qquad P_S^\pm := \frac{\Id\pm S}{2}.
    56	\end{align*}
    57	The normalization and correlation identities are
    58	\begin{align}
    59	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2 &= \frac12 d_\rho(S,T)^2,
    60	    \tag{normalization}\label{eq:normalization}\\
    61	  d_\rho(S,T)^2
    62	    &= 2-2\Re\tr(ST\rho),
    63	    \tag{operator correlation}\label{eq:operator-correlation}\\
    64	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
    65	    &= 1-\Re\tr(ST\rho).
    66	    \tag{binary correlation}\label{eq:binary-correlation}
    67	\end{align}
    68	Consequently, the conclusion delivered by the quantum linearity argument can
    69	be written either as
    70	\[
    71	  \mathbb E_a\dbin_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a),A(a))^2\leq\delta
    72	\]
    73	or, equivalently, as
    74	\[
    75	  \mathbb E_a d_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a),A(a))^2\leq2\delta.
    76	\]
    77	These are not equivalent to the same bound $\delta$ for the mean squared
    78	state-dependent operator distance.%
    79	\footnote{The formal declarations are \leanid{binaryObservableEffect},
    80	\leanid{binaryObservableDistSq},
    81	\leanid{binaryObservableDistSq\_eq\_stateDepDistSq\_div\_two},
    82	\leanid{stateDepDistSq\_eq\_two\_sub\_two\_mul\_correlation}, and
    83	\leanid{binaryObservableDistSq\_eq\_one\_sub\_correlation} in
    84	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/BooleanFourier.lean}.}

    86	\section{The source calculation}
    87	
    88	Natarajan and Vidick define the distance between two POVMs by summing the
    89	squared state-dependent distances between corresponding square roots
    90	\cite[Section~3.1]{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  For projective measurements the
    91	square roots are the effects themselves.  In the binary case their calculation
    92	expands $P_S^\pm=(\Id\pm S)/2$ and obtains
    93	\[
    94	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
    95	    = 1-\frac12\tr_\rho(ST+TS)
    96	    = \frac12\tr_\rho((S-T)^2).
    97	  \tag{source equation (3)}
    98	\]
    99	This is equation~(3) at lines~903--910 of the in-repository source mirror.%
   100	\footnote{See
   101	\path{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex}, lines~866--912.  The quantum
   102	linearity theorem and its Fourier--Naimark proof are at lines~1074--1112.}
   103	The next line identifies the final expression with the squared state-dependent
   104	operator distance.  The operator-distance definition at lines~873--875 is
   105	printed with $\rho$ occurring twice,
   106	\[
   107	  d_\rho(S,T)^2 = \tr_\rho\big((S-T)^\dagger(S-T)\rho\big),
   108	  \qquad \tr_\rho(X) := \tr(\rho X),
   109	\]
   110	and we read the duplication as typographical, keeping the single $\rho$ of the
   111	definition of $d$ above.  Under that reading the squared state-dependent
   112	operator distance is $\tr_\rho((S-T)^2)$ rather than one half of that
   113	quantity.  Thus the calculation through line~910 is correct and the equality
   114	on line~911 loses a factor of two.
   115	
   116	The Fourier--Naimark proof is consistent with the measurement normalization.
   117	It proves
   118	\[
   119	  \mathbb E_a\operatorname{CON}_{\rho'}(A(a),\mathcal A(a))
   120	  = \frac12+\frac12\mathbb E_{a,b}
   121	       \tr_\rho(A(a)A(b)A(a+b)).
   122	\]
   123	The hypothesis therefore makes the consistency deficit at most $\delta/2$.
   124	For binary projective measurements, the squared measurement distance is twice
   125	that deficit, giving the bound $\delta$ for the squared binary-measurement
   126	distance and the bound $2\delta$ for the squared state-dependent operator
   127	distance.
   128	
   129	\section{A four-point counterexample}
   130	
   131	The bound $\delta$ for the mean squared state-dependent operator distance is
   132	false.  Let $G=(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^2$, choose $r\in G\setminus\{0\}$, take
   133	the one-dimensional state $\rho=1$, and define scalar binary observables by
   134	\[
   135	  A(a)=\begin{cases}
   136	    -1,&a=r,\\
   137	     1,&a\neq r.
   138	  \end{cases}
   139	\]
   140	For the characters $\chi_u(a)=(-1)^{u\cdot a}$, the normalized Fourier
   141	coefficients satisfy
   142	\[
   143	  \widehat A(0)=\frac12,
   144	  \qquad
   145	  \widehat A(u)=-\frac12\chi_u(r)\quad(u\neq0).
   146	\]
   147	Their multiset is
   148	$\{\frac12,\frac12,\frac12,-\frac12\}$, and hence
   149	\[
   150	  \mathbb E_{a,b}A(a)A(b)A(a+b)
   151	    =\sum_u\widehat A(u)^3=\frac14.
   152	\]
   153	The correlation hypothesis therefore holds with $\delta=3/4$.
   154	
   155	Every scalar exact Boolean representation is one of the characters $\chi_u$,
   156	and its mean squared state-dependent operator distance from $A$ is
   157	\[
   158	  \mathbb E_a |A(a)-\chi_u(a)|^2
   159	    =2-2\widehat A(u)\geq1.
   160	\]
   161	Allowing an ancillary space does not reduce this lower bound.  Exact linearity
   162	and the binary-observable relations make the operators $\mathcal A(a)$ a
   163	commuting family of Hermitian involutions.  Their simultaneous spectral
   164	subspaces carry characters of $G$.  Evaluation in any density operator is
   165	therefore a convex combination of the scalar character correlations above, so
   166	the mean squared state-dependent operator distance remains at least $1$.  It
   167	cannot be at most $\delta=3/4$.  By~\eqref{eq:normalization}, the corresponding
   168	mean squared binary-measurement distance has lower bound $1/2$, which is
   169	compatible with the provider's conclusion.
   170	
   171	\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
   172	
   173	The QPBT paper quotes the quantum linearity theorem at lines~711--725 of its
   174	Pauli-basis analysis and defers its proof to Natarajan and Vidick.%
   175	\footnote{See
   176	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   177	lines~711--725.}
   178	The active blueprint expands the conclusion's distance as the state-dependent
   179	operator distance $d$ and states the bound $2\delta$, together with the
   180	equivalent bound $\delta$ for $\dbin$.  The formal theorem
   181	\leanid{exists\_exactly\_linear\_observables} bounds the average over $u$
   182	of \leanid{stateDepDistSq} by $2\delta$, and its companion
   183	\leanid{exists\_exactly\_linear\_observables\_binaryObservableDistSq}
   184	bounds the average of \leanid{binaryObservableDistSq} by $\delta$; the
   185	printed bound $\delta$ for the mean squared state-dependent operator
   186	distance is not reproduced.%
   187	\footnote{See
   188	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}, lines~104--150, and
   189	the two declarations in
   190	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean}.}
   191	
   192	The mathematical content of the theorem is nevertheless available in the
   193	correct normalization.  The stability theorem
   194	\leanid{exists\_exact\_boolean\_representation} assumes the mean squared
   195	state-dependent multiplicative defect
   196	\[
   197	  \mathbb E_{a,b}\, d_\rho\big(A(a)A(b), A(a+b)\big)^2 \le \eta
   198	\]
   199	and produces an ancillary space, a unit vector $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ in it and
   200	an exactly linear family $\{\mathcal A(a)\}$ of binary observables with
   201	$\mathbb E_a\, d_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a), A(a)\otimes\Id)^2 \le \eta$, where
   202	$\rho' = \rho \otimes \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}$.
   203	Its bound rests on an identity rather than an inequality:
   204	\leanid{avg\_stateDepDistSq\_roundedObservable\_eq\_avg\_multiplicativeDefect}
   205	proves that the two averages above coincide, both being $2-2C$ for the
   206	two-query correlation
   207	$C = \mathbb E_{a,b}\Re\tr(A(a)A(b)A(a+b)\rho)$ of the linearity test.%
   208	\footnote{Both declarations are in
   209	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Stability.lean}; the blueprint
   210	records them as \texttt{lem:boolean-representation-stability}.}
   211	The source hypothesis $C \ge 1-\delta$ is therefore exactly the hypothesis of
   212	the stability theorem with $\eta = 2\delta$, and the theorem then yields the
   213	mean squared state-dependent operator distance bound $2\delta$: the corrected
   214	conclusion identified above, with no restriction on $\delta$ and no commutation
   215	assumption on the $A(a)$.  This reparameterization is the entire
   216	content of the repair, and the corrected source-facing statement
   217	\leanid{exists\_exactly\_linear\_observables} is obtained from
   218	\leanid{exists\_exact\_boolean\_representation} by substituting
   219	$\eta = 2\delta$.
   220	
   221	The Boolean Fourier foundation keeps the state-dependent operator distance
   222	unchanged and adds the separately named binary-measurement distance together
   223	with equations~\eqref{eq:normalization}--\eqref{eq:binary-correlation}.  The
   224	statement repair changed the conclusion to mean squared state-dependent
   225	operator distance at most $2\delta$, added the equivalent form with mean
   226	squared binary-measurement distance at most $\delta$, and synchronized the
   227	blueprint; the realigned theorem is proved by the Fourier--Naimark argument,
   228	with the distance/defect relation established as an equality, that is, by the
   229	stability theorem under the reparameterization just described.%
   230	\footnote{The normalization investigation was tracked in
   231	\ghissue{124}; the source-facing statement repair was carried out in
   232	\ghissue{129}.}
   233	
   234	\section{Conclusion}
   235	
   236	The provider's binary-measurement calculation is correct through the factor
   237	$1/2$ in equation~(3), but its final identification with the squared
   238	state-dependent operator distance is incorrect.  The theorem proved by the
   239	Fourier--Naimark argument has mean squared binary-measurement error at most
   240	$\delta$, equivalently mean squared state-dependent operator error at most
   241	$2\delta$.  The four-point example rules out the printed bound $\delta$ for
   242	the mean squared state-dependent operator distance even when arbitrary
   243	ancillary extensions are allowed.  The blueprint theorem and the formal
   244	declarations carry the corrected bounds.

    18	/-- The Naimark column acts as an isometry on the input subspace: `VP = V`. -/

    55	/-- **Partial isometry to unitary extension** (general fact).
    56	
    57	If `V†V = P` where `P` is a projection and `V = VP`, then there exists
    58	a unitary `U` on the full space with `UP = V`.
    59	
    60	This is a standard result in finite-dimensional linear algebra: V is an
    61	isometry from range(P) to V's range, and in finite dimensions any
    62	isometry between subspaces extends to a unitary.
    63	
    64	**Mathlib route**: `LinearIsometry.extend` provides the extension for
    65	linear isometries between inner product spaces. The gap is the
    66	matrix-to-`EuclideanSpace` transport. -/
    67	private lemma partialIsometry_to_unitary
    68	    {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    69	    (V P : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n)
    70	    (hP : MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj P)
    71	    (hVP : V * P = V)
    72	    (hVV : Vᴴ * V = P) :
    73	    ∃ U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ,
    74	      (U : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n) * P = V := by
    75	  classical
    76	  have toEuclideanLin_mul :
    77	      ∀ A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n,
    78	        Matrix.toEuclideanLin (A * B) =
    79	          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).comp (Matrix.toEuclideanLin B) := by
    80	    intro A B
    81	    simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_mul_same (p := (2 : ENNReal)) A B]
    82	  let Pₗ : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Matrix.toEuclideanLin P
    83	  let Vₗ : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Matrix.toEuclideanLin V
    84	  let S : Submodule ℂ (EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := LinearMap.range Pₗ
    85	  letI : InnerProductSpace ℂ S := Submodule.innerProductSpace S
    86	  have hP_fix : ∀ x : S, Pₗ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) = x := by
    87	    intro x
    88	    rcases x.2 with ⟨y, hy⟩
    89	    rw [← hy]
    90	    calc
    91	      Pₗ (Pₗ y) = (Pₗ.comp Pₗ) y := rfl
    92	      _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (P * P) y := by rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
    93	      _ = Pₗ y := by rw [hP.isIdempotentElem.eq]
    94	  have hVP_lin : Vₗ.comp Pₗ = Vₗ := by
    95	    calc
    96	      Vₗ.comp Pₗ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (V * P) := by rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
    97	      _ = Vₗ := by rw [hVP]
    98	  have hgram : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) = Pₗ := by
    99	    calc
   100	      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) = Matrix.toEuclideanLin P := by rw [hVV]
   101	      _ = Pₗ := rfl
   102	  let Llin : S →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Vₗ.comp S.subtype
   103	  have hLnorm : ∀ x : S, ‖Llin x‖ = ‖x‖ := by
   104	    exact (LinearMap.norm_map_iff_inner_map_map
   105	      (𝕜 := ℂ) (E := S) (E' := EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
   106	      (F := S →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n) Llin).2 fun x y => by
   107	      have hy : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) = y := by
   108	        calc
   109	          Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) =
   110	              Pₗ (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := by rw [hgram]
   111	          _ = y := hP_fix y
   112	      calc
   113	        inner ℂ (Llin x) (Llin y) =
   114	            inner ℂ (Vₗ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) (Vₗ (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) := rfl
   115	        _ = inner ℂ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
   116	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) := by
   117	          dsimp [Vₗ]
   118	          rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
   119	          exact (LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right (𝕜 := ℂ)
   120	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin V) (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
   121	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin V (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n))).symm
   122	        _ = inner ℂ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := by rw [hy]
   123	        _ = inner ℂ x y := rfl
   124	  let L : S →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := { toLinearMap := Llin, norm_map' := hLnorm }
   125	  let Ulin : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n :=
   126	    LinearIsometry.extend (𝕜 := ℂ) (V := EuclideanSpace ℂ n) (S := S) L
   127	  let Umat : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n :=
   128	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm Ulin.toLinearMap
   129	  have hUmat_lin : Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat = Ulin.toLinearMap := by
   130	    exact Matrix.toEuclideanLin.apply_symm_apply Ulin.toLinearMap
   131	  have hUstarU : Umatᴴ * Umat = 1 := by
   132	    apply Matrix.toEuclideanLin.injective
   133	    calc
   134	      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Umatᴴ * Umat) =
   135	          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat).adjoint.comp (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat) := by
   136	            rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
   137	      _ = Ulin.toLinearMap.adjoint.comp Ulin.toLinearMap := by rw [hUmat_lin]
   138	      _ = 1 := by exact Ulin.adjoint_comp_self'
   139	      _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n) := by
   140	            rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_one]
   141	            rfl
   142	  let U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ := ⟨Umat, (Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff').2 hUstarU⟩
   143	  refine ⟨U, ?_⟩
   144	  apply Matrix.toEuclideanLin.injective
   145	  apply LinearMap.ext
   146	  intro x
   147	  have hExt : Ulin (Pₗ x) = Vₗ (Pₗ x) := by
   148	    simpa [Ulin, L, Llin] using
   149	      (LinearIsometry.extend_apply L ⟨Pₗ x, LinearMap.mem_range_self Pₗ x⟩)
   150	  calc
   151	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin ((U : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n) * P) x =
   152	        Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat (Pₗ x) := by
   153	          rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
   154	          rfl
   155	    _ = Ulin (Pₗ x) := by
   156	          rw [hUmat_lin]
   157	          rfl
   158	    _ = Vₗ (Pₗ x) := hExt
   159	    _ = Vₗ x := by
   160	          have hx := congrArg
   161	            (fun f : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n => f x) hVP_lin
   162	          simpa [LinearMap.comp_apply] using hx
   163	    _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin V x := rfl

+	(\texttt{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099--1110}). Let
+	$\{O(a)\}_{a \in \F_2^t}$ be binary observables on a finite-dimensional
+	Hilbert space $\hilb$, with characters $\chi_u$ and Fourier coefficients
+	$\widehat{O}^u$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}, and let
+	$\{B^u = (\widehat{O}^u)^2\}_{u \in \F_2^t}$ be the Fourier-square
+	measurement of Lemma~\ref{lem:fourier-square-measurement}. Write
+	$\hilb' = \C^{\F_2^t \sqcup \{\bot\}}$ for the auxiliary space of
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper} and
+	$\ket{\mathrm{anc}} = \ket{\bot} \in \hilb'$ for its initial vector, so
+	that $\|\ket{\mathrm{anc}}\| = 1$ and
+	$\ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}$ is the auxiliary projector of that
+	lemma. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper} to $\{B^u\}$ yields
+	projections $\{\hat{P}_a\}_{a \in \F_2^t \sqcup \{\bot\}}$ on
+	$\hilb \ot \hilb'$ with $\sum_a \hat{P}_a \le \Id$ --- a projective
+	submeasurement, not a measurement --- and such that, for every operator
+	$X$ on $\hilb$ and every $u \in \F_2^t$,
+	\[
+		\Tr\big((X \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}) \, \hat{P}_u\big)
+		= \Tr\big(X \, B^u\big) .
+	\]
+	Define the rounded family $\{C^u\}_{u \in \F_2^t}$ by enlarging the zero
+	outcome to the complement of the nonzero ones,
+	\[
+		C^u =
+		\begin{cases}
+			\Id - \sum_{v \ne 0} \hat{P}_v & \text{if } u = 0, \\
+			\hat{P}_u & \text{otherwise,}
+		\end{cases}
+	\]
+	and set $\mathcal{L}^a = \sum_u \chi_u(a) \, C^u$ for $a \in \F_2^t$. Then
+	every $C^u$ is an orthogonal projection, $\sum_u C^u = \Id$, and
+	$C^u C^v = 0$ for $u \ne v$; hence $\{C^u\}$ is a projective measurement
+	with outcomes in $\F_2^t$ on $\hilb \ot \hilb'$, whose compression along
+	$\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ is $\{B^u\}$: for every operator $X$ on $\hilb$ and
+	every $u \in \F_2^t$,
+	\[
+		\Tr\big((X \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}) \, C^u\big)
+		= \Tr\big(X \, B^u\big) .
+	\]
+	Moreover $\mathcal{L}^0 = \Id$, each $\mathcal{L}^a$ is a binary
+	observable, the linearity
+	\[
+		\mathcal{L}^a \, \mathcal{L}^b = \mathcal{L}^{a+b}
+	\]
+	holds exactly for all $a, b \in \F_2^t$, and for every operator $X$ on
+	$\hilb$ and every $a \in \F_2^t$,
+	\[
+		\Tr\big((X \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}) \,
+		\mathcal{L}^a\big)
+		= \Tr\Big(X \sum_u \chi_u(a) \, B^u\Big) .
+	\]
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+	\leanok
+	\uses{lem:boolean-characters, lem:boolean-fourier-transform,
+		lem:fourier-square-measurement, lem:naimark-helper}
+	Projections summing to at most the identity are mutually orthogonal, so
+	$\hat{P}_a \hat{P}_b = 0$ for $a \ne b$. Consequently
+	$Q = \sum_{v \ne 0} \hat{P}_v$ absorbs each of its summands on either
+	side, $Q \hat{P}_v = \hat{P}_v Q = \hat{P}_v$ for $v \ne 0$, whence $Q$ is
+	itself a projection and $C^0 = \Id - Q$ is a projection orthogonal to
+	every $\hat{P}_v$ with $v \ne 0$. Splitting off the zero outcome in
+	$\sum_u C^u$ leaves $(\Id - Q) + Q = \Id$.
+
+	For $u \ne 0$ the compression identity is the expectation-preservation
+	identity supplied with the dilation of Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper},
+	rewritten with unnormalized traces; the normalizing factors of the two
+	spaces cancel, the enlarged space having dimension
+	$(\lvert \F_2^t \rvert + 1)$ times that of $\hilb$. For $u = 0$,
+	linearity of the trace reduces the claim to
+	$\Tr(X \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}) = \Tr(X)$ together with
+	the identity $B^0 = \Id - \sum_{v \ne 0} B^v$, which is the completeness
+	$\sum_u B^u = \Id$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}.
+
+	Expanding $\mathcal{L}^a \mathcal{L}^b$ and using that $C^u C^v$ vanishes
+	for $u \ne v$ and equals $C^u$ for $u = v$ leaves the diagonal terms
+	$\sum_u \chi_u(a) \chi_u(b) \, C^u$, and
+	$\chi_u(a) \chi_u(b) = \chi_u(a+b)$ by
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-characters}. Taking $a = 0$ in the definition of
+	$\mathcal{L}^a$ and using $\chi_u(0) = 1$ gives
+	$\mathcal{L}^0 = \sum_u C^u = \Id$. Hermiticity of $\mathcal{L}^a$ follows
+	from the realness of the characters and the self-adjointness of the
+	$C^u$, and $(\mathcal{L}^a)^2 = \mathcal{L}^{a+a} = \mathcal{L}^0 = \Id$
+	because $a + a = 0$ in characteristic two, so each $\mathcal{L}^a$ is a
+	binary observable. The last identity is the compression identity for the
+	$C^u$ summed against the characters.
+\end{proof}

+	\label{lem:boolean-representation-stability}

+		lem:naimark-helper, lem:naimark-rounding}
+	This is not a named statement of \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; it records
+	the conclusion that the Fourier--Naimark argument given there for
+	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}
+	(\texttt{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096--1112}) establishes, with
+	the correlation hypothesis replaced by the mean multiplicative defect of
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity}. Let $t$ be a positive integer, let
+	$\eta \ge 0$, let $\rho$ be a density operator on $\hilb$, and let
+	$\{\mathcal{O}^u\}_{u \in \F_2^t}$ be binary observables on $\hilb$ with
+	\[
+		\E_{u,u'} \, d_\rho\big(\mathcal{O}^u \, \mathcal{O}^{u'},\
+		\mathcal{O}^{u+u'}\big)^2 \le \eta .
+	\]
+	Then there are a finite-dimensional space $\hilb'$, a unit vector
+	$\ket{\mathrm{anc}} \in \hilb'$ and binary observables
+	$\{\mathcal{L}^u\}_{u \in \F_2^t}$ on $\hilb \ot \hilb'$ such that
+	$\mathcal{L}^u \mathcal{L}^{u'} = \mathcal{L}^{u+u'}$ for all
+	$u, u' \in \F_2^t$ and, writing
+	$\rho' = \rho \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}$, which is again a
+	density operator,
+	\[
+		\E_u \, d_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^u,\ \mathcal{O}^u \ot
+		\Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2 \le \eta .
+	\]
+	The bound is the specialization of the identity
+	\[
+		\E_u \, d_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^u,\ \mathcal{O}^u \ot
+		\Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2
+		= \E_{u,u'} \, d_\rho\big(\mathcal{O}^u \, \mathcal{O}^{u'},\
+		\mathcal{O}^{u+u'}\big)^2 ,
+	\]
+	which holds for the family constructed below and whose two sides both
+	equal $2 - 2 \, C_\rho(\mathcal{O})$ for the two-query correlation
+	$C_\rho(\mathcal{O})$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity}.
+
+	This is the mathematical content of Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}: the
+	ancillary space and state are produced explicitly, and by
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity} a correlation hypothesis
+	$C_\rho(\mathcal{O}) \ge 1 - \delta$ is exactly the hypothesis above with
+	$\eta = 2\delta$. The conclusion obtained from such a hypothesis is
+	therefore the bound $2\delta$, which is the bound displayed in
+	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}; the constant $2$ separating it from the bound
+	$\delta$ printed in the source is the normalization recorded in
+	Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}. The present statement is
+	the defect-parameterized form of that theorem, and the substitution
+	$\eta = 2\delta$ is the whole of the proof of
+	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} from it.
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+	\leanok
+	\uses{lem:binary-measurement-distance, lem:blr-defect-identity,
+		lem:fourier-square-measurement, lem:naimark-rounding}
+	Let $\hilb'$ have orthonormal basis indexed by $\F_2^t$ together with one
+	extra element $\bot$, and take $\ket{\mathrm{anc}} = \ket{\bot}$, the
+	initial state of the auxiliary register in the one-measurement Naimark
+	construction of Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper}. Apply that construction to
+	the Fourier-square POVM $\{B^u\}$ of
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:fourier-square-measurement}. It returns
+	projectors indexed by $\F_2^t \cup \{\bot\}$; the residual projector at
+	$\bot$ is folded into the outcome $u = 0$, so that the resulting family
+	$\{C^u\}_{u \in \F_2^t}$ is still a family of orthogonal projectors summing
+	to $\Id_{\hilb \ot \hilb'}$ and still compresses to $B^u$ along
+	$\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$, the latter because $\sum_u B^u = \Id_\hilb$. Set
+	$\mathcal{L}^a = \sum_u \chi_u(a) \, C^u$; orthogonality of the $C^u$ and
+	multiplicativity of the characters give
+	$\mathcal{L}^a \mathcal{L}^b = \mathcal{L}^{a+b}$ and
+	$(\mathcal{L}^a)^2 = \Id$, and each $\mathcal{L}^a$ is Hermitian because
+	the characters are real. Since $\rho'$ is a density operator and both
+	$\mathcal{L}^a$ and $\mathcal{O}^a \ot \Id_{\hilb'}$ are binary
+	observables, Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance} gives
+	\[
+		d_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^a, \mathcal{O}^a \ot \Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2
+		= 2 - 2 \, \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{L}^a \,
+		(\mathcal{O}^a \ot \Id_{\hilb'}) \, \rho'\big) ,
+	\]
+	and taking the adjoint of the triple product, absorbing
+	$\mathcal{O}^a \ot \Id_{\hilb'}$ into the weight and compressing
+	$\mathcal{L}^a$ along $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ rewrites the trace as
+	$\Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^a \, (\sum_u \chi_u(a) B^u) \, \rho\big)$.
+	Averaging over $a$ and applying the overlap and cubic identities of
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:fourier-square-measurement} turns the average into
+	$2 - 2 \, C_\rho(\mathcal{O})$, which is the mean multiplicative defect by
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity}. No commutation among the
+	$\mathcal{O}^u$ is used. The hypothesis then bounds the average by $\eta$.
+\end{proof}

    12	
    13	The **one-measurement Naimark lemma** (`OneMeasNaimarkLemma`) is the
    14	building block: any submeasurement can be dilated to a projective
    15	submeasurement on a space enlarged by one auxiliary register.

    17	The questionwise **Naimark interface** (`NaimarkStatement`) records the

    22	The source theorem form is recorded separately as

    27	paper's one-measurement helper.  The proof is the tensor-product assembly

   626		every $C^u$ is an orthogonal projection, $\sum_u C^u = \Id$, and
   627		$C^u C^v = 0$ for $u \ne v$; hence $\{C^u\}$ is a projective measurement
   628		with outcomes in $\F_2^t$ on $\hilb \ot \hilb'$, whose compression along
   629		$\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ is $\{B^u\}$: for every operator $X$ on $\hilb$ and
   630		every $u \in \F_2^t$,
   631		\[
   632			\Tr\big((X \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}) \, C^u\big)
   633			= \Tr\big(X \, B^u\big) .
   634		\]
   635		Moreover $\mathcal{L}^0 = \Id$, each $\mathcal{L}^a$ is a binary
   636		observable, the linearity
   637		\[
   638			\mathcal{L}^a \, \mathcal{L}^b = \mathcal{L}^{a+b}
   639		\]
   640		holds exactly for all $a, b \in \F_2^t$, and for every operator $X$ on
   641		$\hilb$ and every $a \in \F_2^t$,
   642		\[
   643			\Tr\big((X \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}) \,
   644			\mathcal{L}^a\big)
   645			= \Tr\Big(X \sum_u \chi_u(a) \, B^u\Big) .
   646		\]
   647	\end{lemma}
   648	\begin{proof}
   649		\leanok
   650		\uses{lem:boolean-characters, lem:boolean-fourier-transform,
   651			lem:fourier-square-measurement, lem:naimark-helper}
   652		Projections summing to at most the identity are mutually orthogonal, so
   653		$\hat{P}_a \hat{P}_b = 0$ for $a \ne b$. Consequently
   654		$Q = \sum_{v \ne 0} \hat{P}_v$ absorbs each of its summands on either
   655		side, $Q \hat{P}_v = \hat{P}_v Q = \hat{P}_v$ for $v \ne 0$, whence $Q$ is
   656		itself a projection and $C^0 = \Id - Q$ is a projection orthogonal to
   657		every $\hat{P}_v$ with $v \ne 0$. Splitting off the zero outcome in
   658		$\sum_u C^u$ leaves $(\Id - Q) + Q = \Id$.
   659	
   660		For $u \ne 0$ the compression identity is the expectation-preservation
   661		identity supplied with the dilation of Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper},
   662		rewritten with unnormalized traces; the normalizing factors of the two
   663		spaces cancel, the enlarged space having dimension
   664		$(\lvert \F_2^t \rvert + 1)$ times that of $\hilb$. For $u = 0$,
   665		linearity of the trace reduces the claim to
   666		$\Tr(X \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}) = \Tr(X)$ together with
   667		the identity $B^0 = \Id - \sum_{v \ne 0} B^v$, which is the completeness
   668		$\sum_u B^u = \Id$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}.
   669	
   670		Expanding $\mathcal{L}^a \mathcal{L}^b$ and using that $C^u C^v$ vanishes
   671		for $u \ne v$ and equals $C^u$ for $u = v$ leaves the diagonal terms
   672		$\sum_u \chi_u(a) \chi_u(b) \, C^u$, and
   673		$\chi_u(a) \chi_u(b) = \chi_u(a+b)$ by
   674		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-characters}. Taking $a = 0$ in the definition of
   675		$\mathcal{L}^a$ and using $\chi_u(0) = 1$ gives
   676		$\mathcal{L}^0 = \sum_u C^u = \Id$. Hermiticity of $\mathcal{L}^a$ follows
   677		from the realness of the characters and the self-adjointness of the
   678		$C^u$, and $(\mathcal{L}^a)^2 = \mathcal{L}^{a+a} = \mathcal{L}^0 = \Id$
   679		because $a + a = 0$ in characteristic two, so each $\mathcal{L}^a$ is a
   680		binary observable. The last identity is the compression identity for the
   681		$C^u$ summed against the characters.
   682	\end{proof}
